shared_unknowns.S: bijection on Z_256 (256 byte values, constrained to be a permutation)
shared_unknowns.S_inv: inverse of S (not independent -- determined by S)
shared_unknowns.pi: permutation of {0..n-1} (byte-position permutation), fixed for a given (h,w,c)
shared_unknowns.a: n bytes in Z_256 (forward diffusion stream)
shared_unknowns.b: n bytes in Z_256 (backward diffusion stream)

per_message_known.p_i: n known plaintext bytes (chosen/known by the attacker)
per_message_known.c_i: n known ciphertext BODY bytes (header/nonce/tag excluded per experimental validity rules)

per_message_derived_not_free.c_i_k: S[(u_i_k + c_i_{k+1} + b_k) mod 256], c_i_n = iv_b

key_structural_fact: u^(i) and c^(i) are deterministic functions of (S, pi, a, b, iv_f, iv_b, p^(i)); they are not independent free variables. The problem is a constraint-satisfaction search over (S, pi, a, b, iv_f, iv_b), not a linear system to invert.
equations_per_message: 2n byte-equality constraints (n forward S-applications implicitly checked via the final backward output matching c_i exactly over all n positions)

bijectivity_constraints.S: 256 values must be a permutation of {0..255} (S injective & total)
bijectivity_constraints.pi: n values must be a permutation of {0..n-1}

cross_message_sharing: S, pi, a, b, iv_f, iv_b are IDENTICAL across all M messages (this is the nonce-reuse premise); only p^(i) (hence q^(i), u^(i), c^(i)) vary per message.
success_criterion: NOT exact recovery of (S, pi, a, b, iv_f, iv_b). Success = recovering ANY tuple (possibly a different, functionally-equivalent tuple) that correctly predicts c^(target) from p^(target), or equivalently decrypts an unseen c^(target) to the correct p^(target), for a message not among the known pairs.
